title: Reason Code 49 — no connection request policy matched
plain_english: The request was rejected one layer earlier than usual: it didn't match any Connection Request Policy, so NPS never even evaluated network policies or credentials. CRPs filter on how/where the request arrived — day and time, NAS address, port type — not on who the user is.

any: did not match any connection request policy

causes.cause: The default 'Use Windows authentication for all users' CRP was deleted, disabled, or reordered below a non-matching one.
causes.next_check: In the NPS console under Connection Request Policies, confirm an enabled policy whose conditions cover this request (the default matches everything, all day).

causes.cause: A CRP condition is too narrow — day/time restrictions or a specific NAS IPv4 address that this NAS doesn't match.
causes.next_check: Compare this event's NAS IPv4 Address and timestamp against each CRP's conditions.

causes.cause: The request was meant to be forwarded to another RADIUS server (proxy scenario) and the forwarding CRP doesn't cover it.
causes.next_check: If you proxy by realm, check the User Name's realm/suffix in this event against the CRP's realm-matching rules.
